body.p: The history of the Pyak family This legend was told to me by Oka Pyak, the Tar Tree. Pyak moved quickly, apparently running away from something. Various interesting places were left behind him as the poor man ran away. He came to a large lake and put his tent there. He saw that there were many birds and animals on both sides of the lake. And there he began to live. They were living like that for a while and he had two sons, An and Piv. One morning the man says, "I'm going to a distant land to hunt." He caught a deer and got ready to go hunting in a distant land. And his wife says: "Stay still, don't go, our lands are restless now, someone will find you." He went away, but his wife is still waiting for him. But her husband is still missing. She had to live there on her own. She goes hunting by herself, fishes by herself, and raises her children on the shore of that big lake. That is how she lives. Her children had grown up. One day they went hunting with small bows made by their mother. Waders are hunted on their lake, small teals are hunted by them. As time went on, the children got a little older and one day they found their father's boat covered with holes. And they say, "What could it be?" They went to their mother and said, "What is it?" And their mother says, "It's your father's boat, it's the boat you sail on the water. There are oars and a boat." There are oars and a boat. The sons consulted with each other and said, "Let's make one." They went to their mother and said, "How do you make a boat?" Their mother says, "Here are father's tools: in the sledge. Use them to make a boat, and I'll tell you how. So the two sons started to build a boat together. They cut down the wood for the boat, stripped it of its bark, and began to cut out the inside. The sticks at both ends were smeared with charcoal. They hammered these sticks into the boat from the lower side so that the boat would be of the same thickness, began to build the boat edges, then poured the fish soup with the fat of guts inside the boat. Then they put it to the fire to warm up and spread the edges little by little. Cross sticks were made. Then another boat was made. Now the two of them go hunting and fishing on boats, and finally, they are all grown up now. One day they say to their mother: "Mother, there are no people around us at all. And their mother says: "People are far away." At that time the sons collected many animal skins. At the beginning of spring, when the ice was still strong, they went to look for people. They found, bought for the animal skins two deer, a deer cow and a weasel. They lived like that for some years: their deer cow gave birth to two deer for the sledges. Then they went to those people again, took animal skins, the sledge was full of skins. From there they came and brought two girls with them. They started to live on the shore of that lake and gave birth to children. The ornament of the Pyak family Tar Tree is a spruce branch. The family tree of the Pyak family that brings good luck is a spruce. The spirit of the Shepya is a sable, bringing good luck. The painting they have has the appearance of a sable.
